threads.thread_goal: Align on pilot scope, asset selection, and success criteria.

messages.text: Team, kicking off the Cross-Plant Predictive Maintenance Rollout project. The main goal is to reduce unplanned downtime by standardizing our maintenance approach. First step is to define the pilot scope. I've created a draft Asset Criticality Matrix in A1 to help us select equipment for the first two lines. Please review and add your thoughts. We also need to define the success criteria for the pilot as part of T1 and T7.

Thanks for kicking this off. I've reviewed A1. My vote is for the CNC mills on Line 5 and the primary stamping press on Line 7. They are our biggest downtime offenders and have the most potential for quick wins. For KPIs, I suggest we track: 1. Unplanned Downtime (%), 2. Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF), and 3. Maintenance Schedule Compliance. We can track these in A6.

I agree with the asset selection. The stamping press on Line 7 is a good candidate, but we need to be aware that its existing vibration sensors are old. The data quality might be insufficient for accurate predictive models, which is one of the project risks. We might need a small budget for sensor upgrades there. The CNC mills are fine, their controllers are modern.
The KPIs sound right. I can start putting together the tracking sheet A6 with those metrics right away. Should I add any others, like Mean Time to Repair (MTTR)?
Good question. Let's stick to the three main ones for the pilot to keep it focused. We can add MTTR later when we scale. Thanks for taking the lead on A6.
Hi all. Sorry for the delay. What criteria are we using in A1 to define 'criticality'? I want to make sure I understand.
The choices seem fine to me.
Hi, the criteria are on the first tab of A1. It's a combination of production impact, historical failure rate, and safety considerations. Let me know if it's not clear.

Good point on the sensors, @18383. Let's proceed with the stamping press for the pilot but flag the sensor upgrade as a potential follow-up action in the final report. We can't let it block the pilot, given the budget constraints.
Ok, I see it now. Thanks.

Sounds like we have a consensus. Let's formalize the decisions.
1. We approve the CNC mills on Line 5 and the stamping press on Line 7 for the pilot. (D1)
2. The primary KPIs for the pilot will be Unplanned Downtime, MTBF, and Maintenance Schedule Compliance. (D2)

Does anyone object?
Confirmed. I'll update the project charter.
Agreed.
Confirmed. I'll finalize the setup of A6 today.
Excellent. Decisions D1 and D2 are locked. I will finalize the asset list for T1. @36422, you own the final definition for T7.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalize the standardized predictive maintenance workflow.

messages.text: Hi team, following up on our pilot scope discussion, I've mapped the current maintenance workflows (T2) and drafted a new standardized process in A2. The goal is to have a single, clear procedure from alert to resolution. Please review the proposed flow and especially the escalation paths. Feedback is welcome.

Thanks @36422, I've just read through A2. It looks much cleaner than the current process. One question: for a Level 2 alert, who is officially responsible for the handoff from the line operator to the maintenance tech? The diagram is a little ambiguous there.

This is a solid proposal. I'd suggest adding a specific triage step at the beginning to differentiate between mechanical and electrical alerts. For electrical issues, it's critical to involve someone with the right qualifications early to avoid wasted time and ensure safety. We can define specific trigger conditions for that.
Who needs to update the maintenance log in the system when the work is done? Is it the tech or the supervisor?

Great work, @36422. This level of standardization is exactly what we need. The clear role definitions are key to preventing confusion on the shop floor. @18383's point about electrical triage is important.
This new process seems to have a lot of steps. Will we get training on it?
Yes, absolutely. A full training plan is part of T6. No one will be expected to follow the new process without proper training and support materials.

With those clarifications, let's confirm the core responsibilities for alert response. Proposal: Level 1 alerts (initial triage) are handled by Line Supervisors. Level 2 alerts (requiring intervention) are assigned to the on-shift Maintenance Tech. Can we agree on this? This is for D4.
Agreed. That makes sense.
Works for me.
Perfect. Then we can consider the process signed off. I'll incorporate the feedback into a final version of A2 and share it by end of day. Thanks everyone for the input.

threads.thread_goal: Lock down sensor specs, installation plan, and safety procedures.

messages.text: Team, I've completed the gap analysis for instrumentation on our pilot assets and drafted the sensor and data requirements in A4. This covers the required signals, sampling frequencies, and some notes on installation (T4). I'd appreciate feedback on feasibility, especially regarding integration with existing control systems (T11).

Thanks, @18383. The spec in A4 looks comprehensive. From an operations perspective, my main concern is scheduling. What's your estimate for installation time per asset? We need to fit this into our planned maintenance windows without disrupting production.
Do these new sensors need any special tools for installation? I need to check if my team in the garage has them.
This looks good. Can you confirm that the cost for the proposed hardware in A4 is within the limited capex budget we discussed? We need to be careful with spending here.
While we're on installation, who is responsible for the safety checklist (T8)? We need to make sure we have that ready before any work starts.
That's T8, my task. I can start a draft for the checklist A3, but I'll need some help with the specific electrical safety steps and lockout/tagout procedures for these new sensors.
Happy to help, @237177. I can provide all the necessary electrical safety details. Let's collaborate on A3 and get it done by tomorrow.

Great. It sounds like we have a clear path forward. Let's make a decision. Can we formally approve the sensor and data collection spec as documented in A4? (D5). And can we agree on the installation plan: work will be done during scheduled maintenance windows using the safety checklist A3, which @18383 and @237177 will finalize by EOD tomorrow? (D6)
Approved from my side.
I approve. We'll get A3 finalized as planned.
Ok, sounds good.
Decisions D5 and D6 are confirmed. Let's move forward.

threads.thread_goal: Coordinate pilot go-live, training, and daily status updates.

messages.text: Alright team, we are one week away from the pilot go-live. This thread is for final coordination of the rollout (T9). We need to lock in the installation schedule (T5) and the training sessions (T6). Let's get everything confirmed by end of day.

I've already aligned with production planning. The maintenance windows for next Tuesday and Wednesday are confirmed and blocked on the shared calendar. This means our go-live date is set for next Thursday. Let's confirm this as our official date (D7).

Great. I've drafted the training schedule based on the materials in A5. Proposal: 
- Session 1 (Maintenance/Garage): Monday @ 10am
- Session 2 (Line 5 Operators): Monday @ 2pm
- Session 3 (Line 7 Operators): Tuesday @ 9am
Please let me know if these times work for your teams.
My garage team can make the Monday 10am session. Thanks.
Are the training materials in A5 final? I haven't had a chance to look at them yet.
Yes, they were finalized last week. The link is in the channel header. They are ready for the sessions.
The schedule works for the maintenance and operations teams. Thanks for setting that up, @560411.

Okay, let's lock it all in. 
- Decision D7: Pilot go-live is confirmed for next Thursday, with installation happening in the maintenance windows on Tuesday and Wednesday.
- Decision D8: The training dates proposed by @560411 are approved. All relevant teams must attend their assigned session.

Any final concerns before we proceed?
Looks solid. Let's do it.
I'll be on standby during the installation windows to support the maintenance team if any electrical issues come up.
Great. Decisions are made. I will post a daily status update here during installation week. We'll use the A6 sheet to track performance from go-live onwards. Let's make this a smooth rollout.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot results, customer impact, and decide on rollout roadmap.

messages.text: Team, the pilot period has concluded. I've compiled the performance data from A6 and drafted a lessons learned report in A7. Please take a look. Overall, the results are very positive, and I want to thank everyone for their hard work. Now it's time to discuss the findings (T10) and plan our full rollout (A8).

Great summary in A7. The 15% reduction in unplanned downtime on the pilot lines is a fantastic result. One key learning for me was that having Line Supervisors handle the initial alert triage (our decision D4) created a bottleneck. For the scale-up, I strongly recommend we create a dedicated Maintenance Coordinator role to own this. This would streamline the process significantly.

I did an informal check with the aftersales team as part of T12. They said they anecdotally had fewer service calls related to the pilot machines, which is good news. I don't have specific numbers though.

Looking at the data in A6, I noticed the vibration sensor on the stamping press gave us a few false positives. As I suspected, the data quality wasn't ideal. For the full rollout, we should either use a different sensor model for that asset type or develop a software filter. This might mean we need to adjust our initial asset list for the next phase (revisiting D1).
Where can I find the draft of the rollout roadmap A8?
@55217 We will create the roadmap A8 based on the outcome of this discussion. It doesn't exist yet.

Excellent points, all. @36422, I completely agree about the triage role. Let's make that a formal decision: we will revise the process to include a dedicated Maintenance Coordinator for alert triage (revisiting D4). Can you draft a short role description for the rollout plan?

@18383, great catch on the sensor data. We must act on that. Let's also decide to adjust the asset scope for the scale-up (revisiting D1). We will prioritize assets where we have high-confidence sensor data and create a separate workstream to validate sensors for other critical machines.
Will do. I'll have a draft role description by tomorrow.

Perfect. So, to summarize our decisions: we are adjusting the asset scope for the full rollout based on sensor performance (D1), and we are redesigning the triage process around a new coordinator role (D4). I will incorporate these key decisions into the final pilot report A7 and begin drafting the Cross-Functional Rollout Roadmap A8. Thanks again for a successful pilot.
